paper_title: Before Generation, Align it! A Novel and Effective Strategy for   Mitigating Hallucinations in Text-to-SQL Generation
caption: Results of different schema linking modules on BIRD-dev.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three different schema linking modules — DIN-SQL (zero-shot), TA-SQL (zero-shot), and DIN-SQL (few-shot) — on the BIRD-dev dataset, measured across three evaluation metrics: Recall, Precision, and F1 Score. The vertical axis represents the score percentage, ranging from 40 to 100, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The horizontal axis lists the three metrics, each with three grouped bars corresponding to the three methods, color-coded as light blue for DIN-SQL (zero-shot), dark blue for TA-SQL (zero-shot), and light green for DIN-SQL (few-shot). For Recall, scores are 63.58 (DIN-SQL zero-shot), 71.90 (TA-SQL zero-shot), and 72.29 (DIN-SQL few-shot). For Precision, scores are 88.89, 91.24, and 92.31 respectively. For F1 Score, scores are 75.34, 80.40, and 81.08 respectively. Across all metrics, DIN-SQL (few-shot) consistently achieves the highest scores, followed by TA-SQL (zero-shot), and then DIN-SQL (zero-shot), indicating that the few-shot variant of DIN-SQL outperforms the others on this benchmark.
